headline: Approved a $200,000 loan to White Birch Living, LLC and increases to elderly, disabled, and blind tax exemption amounts.
summary: The loan is for a local business that is expanding in Manchester and provides manufacturing jobs. It carries 5.5% interest over ten years and is fully collateralized. Exemption amounts were raised to match the citywide revaluation, and the assessor said the 2025 reductions totaled about $2.338 million in taxes.
decisions: Approved the amended bylaws for the Manchester Arts Commission.

transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON ADMINISTRATION/INFORMATION SYSTEMS

October 20, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Chairman Fajardo called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen Fajardo, Kantor, Bonilla, Kaw-uh, Sapienza

Messrs.: Alderman Terrio, Alderman Trisciani, A. Chhom, C. Kurfehs

1. Communication from Jodie Nazaka, Economic Development Director, requesting approval of the amended bylaws for the Manchester Arts Commission.

On motion of Alderman Kaw-uh , duly seconded by Alderman Bonilla , it was voted to approve.

- 2. Communication from Amy Chhom, Chair of the Manchester Development
- Corporation, requesting approval of a $200,000 Custom MHT Loan to White
- Birch Living, LLC.

Amy Chhom, Chair of the Manchester Development Corporation: I'm the chair of Manchester Development Corp, and on my board is both June and Dana Dexter as the aldermanic committee members. We have Maria Mongan, Secretary, and Steve Shiner, Treasurer here as well.

Alderman Sapienza: Just give us the long and short of it, if you would.

A. Chhom: Well, after a great three years of putting together a brand new strategic plan which was implemented, updating bylaws, putting out loan programs, we're finally able to execute our first large loan after about 15 years, since the time when Manchester Development Corp. was executing loans to redevelop buildings downtown. This particular business, which we won't state publicly, is a local business that was started in Manchester, continues to expand within Manchester, provides manufacturing jobs and we're excited to be able to offer them a $200,000 loan in order to support their expansion. And it is fully collateralized.

Alderman Sapienza: It has your support?

A. Chhom: It has our support unanimously.

Alderman Kaw-uh: For everyone's awareness, everyone in the public, this would not be a loan that's for free. It's not a 0% interest rate loan. It is my understanding it would be 5.5% over ten years. So it's ten years, 5.5% interest rate.

On motion of Alderman Bonilla , duly seconded by Alderman Kantor , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Bonilla , duly seconded by Alderman Sapienza , it was voted to expedite the committee’ s report to the full Board.

3. Communication from Charles Kurfehs, Chairman of the Board of Assessors, recommending that the City's elderly, disabled, and blind exemption benefit amounts be increased to align with the City-wide revaluation.

Alderman Kaw-uh: I was wondering if we could get a tally, I suppose, of the current property tax reductions that are in place now. Could you give a brief overview of how much the city is currently providing in terms of property tax reductions?

Charles Kurfehs, Assessor: The total value of the assessment reduction in 2025 was $115,525,530.

Alderman Kaw-uh: And what would that equate to in terms of dollar amount of property taxes?

C. Kurfehs: In 2025 that number was about $2.338 million.

Alderman Kaw-uh: The only reason I wanted to bring that up, I'm not opposed to this proposal, necessarily, I just want us to be aware that approximately $2 million that the city is providing in tax reductions does also have to come back from somewhere else. And so everyone else who's paying into the property tax system winds up paying for that as well.

Alderman Sapienza: So essentially the math has already been done here, right? In other words, this is increasing incrementally percentage wise. It's not really changing, right?

C. Kurfehs: Right. Exactly. It's adjusting for the increase in the value of the median house and or dwelling in each of the different categories of elderly, disabled, and blind.

Alderman Sapienza: These requirements, it's not strictly done by age. It's done by income and assets as well, right?

C. Kurfehs: Those are the qualifying limits.

Alderman Sapienza: Do you verify the assets?

C. Kurfehs: Yes, we do; extensively.

Alderman Sapienza: You do?

C. Kurfehs: And income as well, including reviewing bank statements, income statements, investment account statements.

Alderman Sapienza: I understand the income verification would be fairly easy, with income tax statements and whatnot. Not so easy with the assets, though. I mean, how do you do that? And again, this is really more out of my own curiosity. I don't want to make a federal case of this, but how do you verify the assets?

C. Kurfehs: Well, the assets, for example, if someone has $100,000 in their 401K and we receive that statement, then we would just put that as an asset. Actually it's normally the income that's more difficult, really.

Alderman Sapienza: Income is more difficult than assets?

C. Kurfehs: Exactly, the reason being is because we get a lot of bank statements that have things like cash deposits. And we've got to try to figure out the source of those deposits. And many times it is not clear.

Alderman Terrio: I was looking at Nashua. So there's three parts to the exemptions, and I'm glad that we're increasing that. Alderman Sapienza just touched upon it, there's also income and assets, that is not changing in this proposal. I looked at Nashua. Nashua has higher income to qualify and higher assets. Are you going to explore that in the near future, modifying those two items? That would be up to your committee to be able to call for something of that nature. I would suggest, if you wish to pursue that, that I would pursue that after the second tax bills go out. It would be impossible right now to change those limits. I would just point out that Nashua has a higher income to qualify and also a higher asset number to qualify for this. Ours is lower. I just wanted to point that out.

Alderman Trisciani: We also have the veterans’ credit, which is $500 off the tax bill. And the disabled is $2,000. Should those be changing as well? Or are those limits in line?

C. Kurfehs: I think in the future, that's something that if the committee wishes to explore, I would encourage it. But the exemptions are more tied towards need and ability to earn income, and so the veterans’ credits are more of a thank you for your service type benefit.

Chairman Fajardo: If a veteran has a disability, there are options that would be tied to that as well. Right?

C. Kurfehs: Yes, that's correct.

Alderman Trisciani: I will leave that with you. I would love to see us explore that a little bit more in the future.

Chairman Fajardo: We talked about this briefly and the board looked at that sort of category of exemptions. My point is to say that we have in the fairly recent past taken a look at those; not to say that we can't do it again, but I know that when you and I were speaking, you were explaining to me that it's important to make sure that we're kind of cycling through all of the different categories of exemptions on a standard cadence.

C. Kurfehs: That's true, absolutely.

Alderman Kaw-uh: I just want us to be cautious of potential changes to the asset amounts and other things like that, because especially the elderly exemptions don't directly benefit working families or younger folks. And if we want to attract and retain younger families in Manchester, something like that may not be the right way to go, but in terms of adjusting these amounts right here in front of us to better reflect the new values, I'd like to make a motion to approve the recommended amounts from the Assessor.

On motion of Alderman Kaw-uh , duly seconded by Alderman Sapienza , it was voted to approve.

On motion of Alderman Kantor , duly seconded by Alderman Kaw-uh , it was voted to expedite the committee’ s report to the full Board.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Sapienza , duly seconded by

Alderman Kantor , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee

- Meeting End Time: 6:42PM
